advances: An actual two-layer example at a strict minimum of the displayed signed one-parameter family. Only the listed finite critical circuit menus are used. The baseline normalized depth 1/4 exceeds the sharp target 2/9.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The base projection is $[0,1]$, so the two sampled fibers are precisely the specified compact sets. The area of $K_t$ is four by vertical integration and hence $M_t=4(1+t)^2+4(1-t)^2$. The raw mixed depth at a point of either fiber equals its ordinary raw depth there. Every ambient cap containing it contains an own-fiber cap through it or the whole own fiber. Conversely any continuous halfspace through it can be extended to a finite ambient halfspace with the same trace and a base tilt large enough to exclude the other compact layer. Taking maxima and scaling the own-fiber areas gives the depth formula. At $t=0$ a square has ordinary depth $1/2$, by symmetry at its center and the upper bound from any opposite pair through a point. The area removed from the square in $K_t$ is $|t|/2$. Since every square cap containing zero has area at least two and zero remains interior to $K_t$, $D(K_t)\ge1/2-|t|/8$. Substitution and expansion in $s=|t|$ gives the stated strict restricted minimum.

For an own-plane cap with inward unit normal $u$ at anchor $p\in\{0,1\}$, take the ambient margin $u\cdot(x,y)-10(1-2p)(z-p)$. The other layer is strictly excluded for all sufficiently small $|t|$, also for nearby thresholds. The three unit continuous normals at each center have positive dependence weights proportional to $(1,1,\sqrt2)$ and cover that plane. Their old section lengths are $(2,2,2\sqrt2)$. The old mixed cap masses are each two. At either square center this is its maximal mixed raw depth, as proved by the depth identity above. The threshold sections at the proper cuts are positive and continuous under the small shape and threshold changes: the square meets the cutting line in a segment, with only its two endpoints on the old boundary, and on translated nearby lines convergence of the section indicators away from those endpoints gives convergence of length. Thus the threshold derivative is the negative old section length with a joint first-order expansion once the fixed-threshold derivative is computed. This verifies the regular response hypothesis of d3c5fb55ec5bc99d, and its reciprocal-section weights are all $1/3$. The circuits have a common old interior mark at each site and constant old mass, as required.

The first two positive cap areas of $K_t$ are $2+t/2$ and $2$ by integration. The cap $x+y\le0$ has area two for $t\le0$. When $t>0$ it loses the triangle between the lines $y=1+tx$ and $y=-x$ over $-1\le x<-1/(1+t)$, of area $t^2/[2(1+t)]$. Its first derivative is therefore zero. The opposite cap derivatives are their negatives because the area of $K_t$ is four. The common-quantile raw mass derivatives for the two circuits on $K_t$ are consequently $\pm1/6$. The first layer's factor $(1+t)^2$ adds four to the raw derivative of each old cap of area two, and the second layer's factor $(1-t)^2$ subtracts four. As $M'_0=0$, subtracting the old normalized ratio times $M'_0$ leaves these centered raw covectors unchanged. Convexifying gives the stated two menus. At weight $q$ on the first, the weighted interval has center $4(2q-1)$ and radius $1/6$. Its maximal absolute value is minimized at $q=1/2$. The frozen game has the negative of this minimum, by the signed unit interval and independent choices. All transversals have opposite signs and hence a positive balance.

statement:
For $|t|<1$ let $K_t=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le1,\ -1\le y\le1+tx\}$. Take the convex hull $C_t$ of the fibers $(1+t)K_t$ and $(1-t)K_t$ at the integer bases $0$ and $1$. Its mixed area is $M_t=8(1+t^2)$. If $D(K_t)$ is ordinary maximal normalized halfspace depth, its actual mixed normalized maximum is
$$
D_{\mathrm{MI}}(C_t)=\frac{(1+|t|)^2}{2(1+t^2)}D(K_t).
$$
It equals $1/4$ at $t=0$ and for $0<s=|t|<1$ exceeds $1/4$ by at least $s(7-2s-s^2)/(16(1+s^2))>0$.

At each of its two old maximizing centers take the two opposite three-cap circuits with own-fiber inequalities $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, $x+y\le0$ and their reversals, extended by strict oblique isolation from the other layer. These are actual regular critical circuits at $t=0$. Along the signed $t$ direction the convexified menus of centered raw common-quantile responses for these choices are $4+[-1/6,1/6]$ and $-4+[-1/6,1/6]$. Every selection balances positively, yet the common frozen-weight game in the absolute-value norm has value $-1/6$ in raw response units, or $-1/48$ after dividing by $M_0$.
title: Actual critical trapezoid menus realize the frozen-weight gap
